verify.note: Reads the migration set with SQL comments stripped and the code with comments stripped: the ledger exists with planned and failed states and one row per seller per order, a transfers module creates transfers under a key fixed to the ledger row, the settle hands a paid split order to it, a reconciler route exists and is scheduled, and the webhook reads a reversal. Fails on main at its first arm. Cannot see the applied state (check:migrations) or a live transfer (Stripe); lib/commerce/transfers.test.ts owns the state machine and the never-twice guarantees.

append.detail: CLOSED 2026-09-29 (ADR-1614). RE-TESTED first on main after LIVE-621 (#3000): no file called `stripe.transfers.create`, no migration created a table holding a transfer, app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts acked every `transfer.*` event through its default arm, and recordCommerceOrderFromSession flipped a separate order to paid and paid nobody. SHIPPED. (1) MIGRATION 20270345009800_commerce_order_transfers.sql, NOT 20270345009610 as this row said (the orchestrator assigned 9800 after LIVE-621 took 9700): `public.commerce_order_transfers`, one row per seller per order (unique order_id + seller_key, the seam sellerKey), owner_kind profile or space only, stripe_account_id, amount_cents > 0 (gross minus fee), platform_fee_cents, currency, status planned | created | failed | reversed with a CHECK that created and reversed rows carry a stripe_transfer_id (unique) and the others do not, source_charge_id, reversed_cents between 0 and amount, attempts, last_error, created_at, updated_at; order_id on delete restrict; owner FK indexes and a partial due-queue index; RLS on with no policy and revoked from anon and authenticated (service role only, like financial_transactions). Gate lists in the same change: rls-deny-all, rls-deny-surface (money, all four commands denied), the pgTAP deny matrix (48 tables), table-grants (internal), lib/database.types.ts by hand in the generated shape. pgTAP: supabase/tests/commerce_order_transfers.test.sql (11 assertions). Authored only, applied to no database by this change. (2) `lib/commerce/transfers.ts`: `planTransferShares` (pure; one share per metadata.split entry, refused whole unless the gross sums to the order amount and the fees to its platform fee, a zero share skipped), `planTransfersForOrder` (upsert, ignoreDuplicates on order_id + seller_key), `executePlannedTransfers` (one row at a time; a compare-and-set claim on attempts; `stripe.transfers.create` with amount, currency, destination, transfer_group = order id, source_transaction = the order charge, metadata carrying the row id, under the idempotency key transfer:<row id>; created with the transfer id or failed with last_error; a retry first looks in the order transfer_group for a transfer carrying its row id and adopts it, and refuses to create when it cannot look), `settleSplitOrderTransfers` (the settle call, never throws), `reconcileTransfers`, `recordTransferCreated`, `recordTransferReversed`, `listOrderTransfers` (the read LIVE-623 and LIVE-624 build on). A seller is paid only while the order is paid or fulfilled with no refund. (3) recordCommerceOrderFromSession hands a separate row it flipped to settleSplitOrderTransfers, after the paid flip and before the stock decrement, once per flip. (4) `app/api/cron/reconcile-transfers/route.ts` (rejectUnauthorizedCron, withCronHeartbeat, cronBudget 100), in vercel.json at 20,50 past each hour: plans a paid split order from the last three days that has no row, retries planned and failed rows under 8 attempts untouched for ten minutes, and logs every row over the ceiling as `commerce.transfer.stuck`, one line each, every run. Registered in lib/observability/slos.ts (every 30 min; unmonitored with its reason, since a Healthchecks check is an account change) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (31 jobs). (5) The webhook: `transfer.created` adopts a transfer whose write was lost; `transfer.reversed` sets reversed_cents from Stripe cumulative amount_reversed (monotonic, so a replay converges) and status reversed once it is all back. OWNER NOTE: both events fire on the platform account, so the platform-scoped Stripe webhook destination must subscribe to them. NOT THE FINANCE LEDGER (ADR-1614 §4, amending ADR-1565 §5 and this row item 2): no financial_transactions payout row per transfer. A split order records its platform fee as commerce revenue, exactly as a destination order records its application fee; a payout row for each seller share against that fee-only row would drive the Labs total negative by every share. The transfer table is the record of money leaving. UNTIL LIVE-623 LANDS a refund of a split order comes from the platform balance while the sellers keep their transfers; a transfer not yet created is held for a refunded order. TESTS: lib/commerce/transfers.test.ts (20, against a stateful table and a stateful Stripe: one transfer per seller; idempotent across a second settle, a reconciler run and a transfer.created redelivery; two concurrent settles make one transfer per seller; a failed transfer is recorded, stops no other seller, and is retried under the same key into exactly one transfer; a create that landed with its answer lost is adopted after the key window; a destination order gets no row and no Stripe call; a refunded order is held; a row over the ceiling is logged stuck; reversals converge), lib/commerce/checkout-funds-flow.test.ts (the settle hands a separate order over, never a destination order, never on a redelivery), app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.test.ts (both transfer events reach the ledger). Mutation-fired: dropping the claim, the adoption lookup or the refunded-order hold each fails a test. PROBE: red on main at its first arm, green here.
